title: Bread, Beer and the Voice Offering
short: The formula continues with the gifts: prt-ḫrw "an invocation offering" of bread and beer, oxen and fowl, linen and alabaster.
trouble: Students read prt-ḫrw as "voice". It means the offering that comes forth at the call of the voice.

blocks.html: After the god, the offering formula (The Offering Formula) lists what the dead person should receive. The list is formulaic, and once you know it you can read the middle of almost any stela.

The formula continues prt-ḫrw “an invocation offering”, literally “a going forth of the voice”, of t ḥnqt “bread and beer”, kꜣw ꜣpdw “oxen and fowl”, šs mnḫt “alabaster and linen” and ḫt nbt nfrt wꜥbt “every good and pure thing”.

head: Egyptian
Meaning
rows: an invocation offering (offerings that come forth at the voice)
alabaster (calcite), for vessels of oils and ointments
blocks.cap: The usual offering list (Gardiner, Excursus B).

blocks.html: The list is often multiplied: ḫꜣ m t ḫꜣ m ḥnqt “a thousand of bread, a thousand of beer”, with the lotus 𓆼 for 1,000 (see Numerals). Bread, beer and the other gifts are usually written with short spellings or with pictures of the goods, because every reader knew the list.

blocks.name: eg-glyphs
blocks.cap: The lotus for 1,000: “a thousand of bread, a thousand of beer…”.

blocks.html: prt means “going forth” and ḫrw “voice”. A prt-ḫrw is the offering that comes forth when the words are spoken. Many stelae address the living: “O you who live on earth, who pass by this stela… say: a thousand of bread and beer for the ka of N”. Speaking the formula was itself an offering.

Why these gifts? They are the necessities and comforts of an Egyptian household: bread and beer for daily food, meat and fowl for feasts, linen for clothing, and stone vessels for oils and perfumes. The dead were expected to need them as the living did, so the formula promised them for eternity.

Reading prt-ḫrw as just “voice”. It is the offering that comes forth at the call of the voice, an invocation offering. Check: ḫrw alone is “voice”; with prt it names a kind of offering, followed by the list of what is offered.
